matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Changing orientation creates shapes that are not representable as Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from a V and placing it vertically to form an I, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere. The total stick count must stay constant.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of planning a move and after each relocation.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a minus sign to make a plus sign without removing any stick from another character.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =). Any shape that does not correspond to one of these is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have decided on a stick relocation, before accepting the transformation.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal, which is not a recognized numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds. A syntactically valid equation that is mathematically false is not a solution.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming the characters are valid, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'XV = XVI - I' as a solution without confirming that the required stick move is possible.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, they must still have both diagonals. A single diagonal is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider removing a diagonal from an X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X, leaving a lone slash.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position within the same numeral, changing its shape (e.g., turning V into X), provided the resulting numeral is valid. This technique can create values not reachable by inter‑character moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a direct transfer does not yield a valid equation but reshaping a numeral might.
matchstick.example: Moving one diagonal of a V to the opposite side to create an X.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot remove a horizontal stick from it or turn it into another operator. The two horizontal sticks must stay together.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving any stick that belongs to the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal bar from '=', leaving a '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Source numeral must retain at least one stick
matchstick.principle: When taking a stick from a numeral, the source numeral must still contain at least one stick so that it remains a recognizable Roman numeral. Removing the sole stick empties the symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before extracting a stick from any numeral.
matchstick.example: Taking the only vertical stick from an I, leaving an empty space.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick between two distinct characters (numeral ↔ numeral, numeral ↔ operator, or operator ↔ operator), ensure that both the source and the destination remain valid symbols after the move. This includes preserving orientation, stick counts, and required shapes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider relocating a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a '-' sign, which empties the I and leaves the '-' unchanged, resulting in an invalid source and destination.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', using uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace. The verifier extracts this line; any deviation leads to rejection.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a valid transformed equation, before sending the final answer.
matchstick.example: Outputting just 'XV = XVI - I' without the required prefix, causing the answer to be ignored.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks that the symbols are valid but forgets to confirm that the numeric values satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides to Arabic numbers and compare after any proposed move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick can unintentionally create or delete an operator (e.g., turning '-' into '+'), altering the number of operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the number and type of operators before and after the move; ensure the count remains unchanged unless the puzzle explicitly allows a change.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a stick from an operator can leave it as an undefined symbol (e.g., turning '=' into '-').
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When taking a stick from an operator, verify that the remaining sticks still form a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Removing the only stick from a numeral
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes extracts the sole stick of an I, leaving an empty symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the source numeral retains at least one stick after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on reasoning and forgets to wrap the final equation in the required 'Correct version of the equation: …' line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After finding a valid equation, explicitly prepend 'Correct version of the equation: ' and output only that line.
